parent_invariant: cmd_subscribe is the only in-tree consumer of the read contract and no unit's boundary names it. It bootstraps its cursor with client.read(channel, i64::MAX, 1) and unwrap_or(0) at cli.rs:200-203; the relay forwards since.max(0); the daemon clamps; the query filters cursor > i64::MAX and returns nothing; and handle_read sets the reply cursor to unwrap_or(since) at idboardd/src/lib.rs:214, echoing i64::MAX back. parent_invariant: Every identity-bearing field on a relayed envelope is filled by the wrapper from its own signer, a peer cannot introduce or override one, and a relayed envelope is byte-for-byte the envelope the daemon authenticates.

local_checks.invariant: RelayRequest has no field under which a peer could express or override a sender identity, sequence number, timestamp, or signature
local_checks.result: RelayRequest is an internally tagged enum with three variants and only v, token, channel, body/since/limit and provenance (wire.rs:44-65). No deny_unknown_fields, so injected keys are discarded, which wire.rs:259-275 asserts directly. dispatch destructures with .. and forwards only channel, body and provenance (relay.rs:124-125). e2e.rs:849-888 injects all five identity fields with a valid token; the post lands as the launching identity with the wrapper's own seq 1, and a second injected seq 1 receives seq 2.

local_checks.invariant: All five identity-bearing envelope fields are filled by the wrapper from its own LocalSigner
local_checks.result: sign_post (keys.rs:143-165) sets sender_id and sender_pubkey_fp from the signer (:153, :154), nonce hardcoded empty (:160), signature filled by finish (:161, :208-214). seq comes from the mutex-guarded SeqCounter (relay.rs:142-146) and timestamp from now_ms() (:148). sign_read (:168-183) sets seq to 0, provenance to NotApplicable and generates a fresh CSPRNG nonce (:178). RelayRequest has no field to introduce one.

local_checks.invariant: A relayed envelope is byte-for-byte the envelope the daemon authenticates
local_checks.result: The signature is computed over canonical length-prefixed bytes, never JSON (keys.rs:210 via envelope.rs:249-251, :197-218), and the daemon recomputes those bytes from the deserialized envelope (keys.rs:296). forward builds DaemonRequest and hands it to round_trip (relay.rs:160-172, ipc lib.rs:268-279) with no post-sign mutation. The only conditionally omitted field is nonce via skip_serializing_if = String::is_empty (envelope.rs:133), restored by the same #[serde(default)], so an empty nonce round-trips to empty.

local_checks.invariant: The child-side client can only emit a RelayRequest and has no daemon fallback
local_checks.result: RelayClient::from_env requires both ENV_RELAY and ENV_TOKEN and fails closed when either is absent (client.rs:47-63); its three senders construct only RelayRequest::Post, ::Read and ::Whoami (:76-103). Test at :159-174 asserts the serialised request contains no identity-bearing field. e2e.rs:448-463 confirms the shipped CLI refuses post, read and whoami with no relay even when the daemon socket is reachable.

local_checks.invariant: The principal the wrapper asserts (Whoami identity) and the principal it signs are one value
local_checks.result: Two sources exist inside Relay: Whoami answers from self.identity (relay.rs:127) while every signed envelope takes sender_id from signer.sender_id() (keys.rs:153), and Relay::new (:78-93) never checks they agree. The only in-tree caller passes &opts.identity and the signer returned by Keystore::load_or_create(&opts.identity) (wrapper.rs:180, :241-247), and load_or_create builds the signer with LocalSigner::from_seed(&seed, identity) using the same string, so no divergence is reachable.

local_checks.invariant: A request the relay cannot honour neither signs an envelope nor advances the replay counter, and a counter gap is not a replay
local_checks.result: post validates channel and body first (relay.rs:139-140) and only then takes a sequence number under the lock (:142-146), so an empty channel, an over-limit channel or an over-long body is refused with BadRequest and burns nothing; relay.rs:304-311 asserts those codes. A request that clears those checks but fails check_op_invariants inside finish does consume a value. SeqCounter never returns zero, negative or a repeat, and the daemon requires strict increase, so the result is a permanent gap, not a reuse.

local_checks.invariant: A peer-supplied field the wrapper signs but cannot verify (provenance) is not treated as a policy input
local_checks.result: provenance is taken verbatim from the request (relay.rs:124) and placed into the signed envelope (keys.rs:157), so a child can sign a claim about its own body's origin. No consumer treats it as authorization or routing input: envelope.rs:76-79 documents it as carried but never enforced, check_op_invariants rejects n/a on a post (:283-285), the store round-trips the string, and the only reader is the terminal renderer.

local_checks.invariant: The wrapper, not the child, owns the ordering and uniqueness of the sequence numbers it signs
local_checks.result: The serve loop is single-threaded: try_accept is drained in a loop and each accepted stream is handled synchronously by serve_one before the next accept or the next 5 ms tick (wrapper.rs:366-377, :393-415). The Mutex around the counter is therefore defensive rather than load-bearing, and the counter advances in strict request order, the precondition for the daemon's strict-increase replay guard.

local_checks.invariant: apply_timeouts must actually install a deadline on an accepted or connected stream on the primary platform
local_checks.result: It does not. apply_timeouts at :181-194 calls set_recv_timeout and set_send_timeout (:183-184) and then discards ErrorKind::Unsupported at :189, returning Ok(()) at :193. On Windows named pipes that Unsupported is the normal, expected outcome, so Ok(()) means no deadline was installed. The doc at :170-180 states this deliberately. accept at :136-138 and connect at :163-168 both route through this function, so no socket in the tree ever carries a deadline on the primary platform.

local_checks.invariant: Every read of peer-controlled bytes in read_frame_from must terminate on its own, independent of the peer sending a newline
local_checks.result: It cannot. read_frame_from at :206-241 loops on reader.fill_buf() at :210 with only three exits: a newline (:222-230), a clean EOF (:215-221), or an error. The only bound on accumulating peer bytes is MAX_FRAME_BYTES at :233-235, a size bound conditional on bytes arriving; a peer that sends zero bytes, or a partial line and then nothing, never trips it. There is no deadline, no attempt counter, no elapsed-time check and no cancellation anywhere in the function.

local_checks.invariant: The same platform limitation must not also remove the deadline on the reply write, the symmetric backpressure path
local_checks.result: It does remove it. set_send_timeout at :184 sits in the same results array and hits the same swallow at :189, so write_all at :262 in write_frame (:256-265) has no send deadline either. A peer that completes its request and then stops reading blocks the writer for as long as it holds the handle open. This makes the write path at crates/idboardd/src/main.rs:194 a one-connection total stall, which is why the board-mutex candidate is not specific to the read side.

local_checks.invariant: The daemon must compensate at its own layer for the platform's missing deadline
local_checks.result: It does not compensate for duration, only for concurrency. The only compensations are the fixed pool (WORKERS=4, :25) and the bounded queue (QUEUE_DEPTH=64, :29, :111). Both bound the number of concurrent workers but bound the duration of a worker's occupancy by nothing. Worse, the compensation the comments describe at :21-24 is undermined at :135, where the single global board mutex is taken before the unbounded read, so one worker blocks all four rather than degrading one.

local_checks.invariant: The test suite must not lock in the no-deadline behaviour as intended on the primary platform

Test applying_timeouts_never_fails_on_either_platform at :423-432 asserts only that apply_timeouts returns Ok, and its comment at :421-422 states the Unsupported path must be tolerated. parent_invariant: An unauthenticated local peer cannot retain a worker slot, the single Board mutex, or the bounded work queue indefinitely, and cannot stop the daemon from serving other identities.

local_checks.invariant: The worker must not acquire the single Arc<Mutex<Board>> before the peer-controlled read, so a stalled connection cannot retain the global board lock
local_checks.result: The order is inverted. The worker loop at :123-141 takes the board lock at :135 and only then calls serve(&mut guard, stream) at :139, passing &mut guard as &mut Board (:168). serve's first peer-facing action is read_frame at :177. So the one global Mutex<Board> created at :117 is held continuously across the entire duration of a peer-paced blocking read. The comment at :114-116 justifies serialising board access but does not note that the critical section is extended over untrusted I/O.

local_checks.invariant: Retention of the single Board mutex by one unauthenticated peer must not stop a different identity's legitimate traffic
local_checks.result: It does. Exactly one Mutex<Board> exists (:117) and it is shared by all four workers (:25, :120-142). While worker 1 holds it, workers 2-4 each pull their own stream at :130 and then block at :135 on the same mutex, pinning three more connections. The accept loop at :146-157 keeps calling tx.send, which on the bounded channel built at :111 blocks once 64 connections are pending (:148); from that point the daemon accepts no connection at all. Because a DIFFERENT identity's legitimate request is served only through this same mutex, this is cross-identity shared availability, not self-harm. Cost to the attacker is one pipe connect and zero crafted bytes; recovery requires the attacker to close.

local_checks.invariant: Every operation inside the board-lock critical section must be bounded by something other than peer cooperation, on both the read and the write side
local_checks.result: Three peer-paced blocking operations sit inside the critical section. read_frame at :177 blocks in BufRead::fill_buf (ipc/lib.rs:210). The rejection log eprintln! at :183 executes while the guard is alive, so a blocked stderr sink also stalls the board. write_frame at :194 blocks in write_all (ipc/lib.rs:262) whenever the peer stops reading; :191 guarantees a DaemonResponse is produced even for an unparseable frame, so the write trigger needs no key and no valid signature at all: send any well-formed line, then never read the reply. This is a second, independent one-connection path to the same total stall.

local_checks.invariant: Moving the lock acquisition to after read_frame must be sufficient, i.e. Board::handle must not itself perform peer-paced blocking I/O
local_checks.result: It must not. Board::handle (:87) delegates to dispatch (:94), whose every branch is local: verify_with_key at :116, store.append at :188, store.read at :209, store.touch at :205 and :230, store.last_seq at :229. No socket, no peer-controlled length beyond the already-framed MAX_FRAME_BYTES and no unbounded loop. So the minimal fix -- move board.lock() to immediately before board.handle(&req) and let read_frame and the log line run outside the guard -- removes all peer-paced blocking from the critical section without changing any security decision.

local_checks.invariant: No other control in the tree bounds per-connection time, replenishes a lost worker, or bounds the queue, such that the accept loop degrades gracefully
local_checks.result: No such control exists. A tree-wide search for catch_unwind returns zero hits, so a panic in serve would kill a worker thread permanently with no respawn (:123-141). Searches for recv_timeout/send_timeout return only the two calls inside apply_timeouts (:183-184), both subject to the Unsupported swallow at :189, so on the primary platform there is no per-connection deadline at all. The queue is bounded but its bound is the saturation point, not a control: tx.send at :148 is an unbounded blocking wait. The poison-recovery paths at :126-129 and :136-138 do correctly recover both locks via into_inner.

local_checks.invariant: The documented risk model for a stalled connection must match what the code actually does
local_checks.result: It does not, which is why this has not been caught. The WORKERS doc at :21-24 and README.md:326-329 both describe the consequence as a stalled client 'occupying a worker' and 'costing throughput rather than the process'. That analysis considers only the four worker slots and overlooks the single Arc<Mutex<Board>> at :117, inside the same critical section. The documented worst case (throughput loss, needs 4 stalled connections) understates the real worst case by an order of magnitude in connections and changes the affected principal from the stalling client to every other identity.
